name: device-comparator-gm-id
description: gm/Id over three decades of drain current and constant-current threshold extraction for the 3.3 V NMOS and PMOS, plus a comparator-input-pair candidate geometry, over the full PVT matrix.
claim: None yet — device characterization ahead of a ratified spec line (#1). Feeds #9 (comparator input-pair sizing) and #14 (Monte Carlo model calibration). Discharges the `V_th ~ 0.7 V [E4]` assumption carried in spec/prior-art-survey.md.

gmid_n_0p2u.description: gm/Id in weak inversion is bounded above by 1/(n*kT/q) — about 38 V^-1 at 27 C for n = 1.0 and lower for any real subthreshold slope factor — and it is proportional to 1/T, so the temperature axis MUST move it by roughly (398-233)/300 ~ 50 %. A weak-inversion gm/Id above 40 V^-1 or a flat temperature axis means the measurement, not the device, is wrong.

gmid_n_100u.description: gm/Id in strong inversion, where it falls as 2/V_ov. The process floor asserts the MOS corner sections reach the transconductance, not just the threshold.

vth_n_l1u.description: constant-current threshold of the 3.3 V NMOS at L = 1 um (V_gs at Id = 100 nA * W/L). Must move with both process and temperature; V_th falls roughly 1-2 mV/K, so -40 -> 125 C is a 10-20 % move.

vth_p_l1u.description: same for the 3.3 V PMOS, reported as |V_th|.

gmid_n_pair.description: gm/Id of the candidate input-pair geometry (W = 40 um, L = 0.5 um) at 10 uA per side — the single number #9 converts into input-referred noise and offset. The band is a plausibility guard, not a spec.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated — gf180mcu ngspice device models (sm141064.ngspice nfet_03v3 / pfet_03v3 subckts from the fets_mm section, mismatch switch off), over the harness's five MOS process corners. No foundry datasheet or literature value is involved.
notes: gm is a finite difference against a 1 mV-offset replica, not ngspice's internal @m[gm] vector: it is the quantity a bench would measure, it survives changes in how the simulator exposes internal device parameters, and it works on the subckt-wrapped devices this PDK ships. 1 mV against ~26 mV of thermal voltage puts the second-order error below 0.1 %.

Threshold uses the constant-current definition V_th = V_gs at Id = 100 nA * (W/L), which is the definition foundry datasheets quote, so these numbers are directly comparable against one. It is NOT the model's internal vth0 parameter and will differ from it.
Bodies are tied to sources. These are zero-Vsb device parameters; whatever body effect a specific comparator topology incurs belongs in #9, not here.

All bias points are diode-connected (Vds = Vgs), i.e. at the edge of saturation. A cascode or a differential pair operating at higher Vds will show slightly higher gm through channel-length modulation; the difference is second order at these lengths but is not zero.
